name: Shecaniah
overview: Shecaniah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known for his role in distributing portions to his fellow Levites. His service in this capacity highlights his involvement in the practical administration of Levitical duties during the post-exilic period. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shecaniah means 'YHWH has taken up his abode,' reflecting a connection to the presence of God. This proper name, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:15, indicates a theologically significant identity tied to God's dwelling.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Shecaniah as a son of Levi, situating him within the Levitical lineage. Beyond this tribal relationship, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Shecaniah's significance lies in his administrative role among the Levites, particularly in the distribution of portions, which was crucial for maintaining the order and function of the priestly tribe. His work ensured that the Levitical community was supported as they carried out their sacred duties, underscoring the importance of faithful stewardship in God's service.
